extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patentees, patent attorneys/agents, and draftspersons preparing U.S. design patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing, filing, and prosecuting a United States design patent application, with emphasis on the drawing disclosure, claim, specification, and procedural practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a design
rubrics_metrics.description: A design consists of the visual ornamental characteristics embodied in, or applied to, an article of manufacture; it may relate to the configuration or shape of an article, to surface ornamentation applied to an article, or to the surface combination of ornamentation. A design for surface ornamentation is inseparable from the article to which it is applied and cannot exist alone; it must be a definite pattern of surface ornamentation applied to an article of manufacture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since a design is manifested in appearance, the subject matter may be configuration/shape, ornamentation, or both. Surface ornamentation must be shown applied to an article (see broken line rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent statutory patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the patent law, design patents are granted for any person who has invented any new, original and ornamental design for an article of manufacture. A design patent protects only the appearance of the article and not structural or utilitarian features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal statutes governing design patents include 35 U.S.C. 171 and related provisions; design patent applicants must satisfy novelty, originality, and ornamentality standards discussed elsewhere (see 35 U.S.C. 102, 103, 112 references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper subject matter for design patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A design dictated primarily by the function of the article lacks ornamentality and is not proper statutory subject matter under 35 U.S.C. 171. A design that simulates a well-known or naturally occurring object or person is not 'original.' Subject matter that could be considered offensive to any race, religion, sex, ethnic group, or nationality is not proper subject matter (35 U.S.C. 171 and 37 CFR § 1.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether there was any unique/distinctive appearance not dictated by function at the time the design was created; if not, likely improper. Also consider statutory and regulatory prohibitions (offensive content).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent and distinct designs must be filed separately; modified forms may be combined
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patent applications may only have a single claim (37 CFR § 1.153). Designs that are independent and distinct must be filed in separate applications; modified forms or embodiments of a single design concept may be filed in one application if their appearance and shape are similar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: eyeglasses and a door handle are independent and require separate applications; two vases with different surface ornamentation creating distinct appearances are distinct; minimal configuration differences that reflect one design concept may be included together (see examples and Page 16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of a design patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: A design patent application should include: (1) Preamble (name of applicant, title, brief description of nature/intended use); (2) Description of the figure(s) of the drawing; (3) Feature description (optional); (4) A single claim; (5) Drawings or photographs; (6) Executed oath or declaration. Filing fee (37 CFR §1.16(f)) is also required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small entity applicants may qualify for fee reductions. Follow the suggested formats to ensure completeness. See 37 CFR §1.154 for arrangement/order of elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The preamble, if included, should state the name of the applicant, the title of the design, and a brief description of the nature and intended use of the article in which the design is embodied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All information in the preamble will be printed on the patent if allowed; therefore the preamble should be accurate and concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the design must identify the article in which the design is embodied by the name generally known and used by the public. Marketing designations are improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specific and descriptive title aids examiner search/classification and helps the public understand the article's nature and use after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure descriptions and permissible specification statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure descriptions should indicate what each view represents (front elevational, top plan, perspective, etc.). Aside from a brief description of the drawing, additional descriptions are generally unnecessary but permissible. Permissible statements include: (1) description of portions not illustrated (e.g., 'right side is mirror image of left side'); (2) disclaiming portions not shown that form no part of the claimed design; (3) statement that broken line illustration of environmental structure is not part of the design; (4) description denoting the nature and environmental use if not in the preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep figure descriptions precise. Use allowed special descriptions when omitting views or using broken lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single claim form and wording
rubrics_metrics.description: A design patent application may include only a single claim. The claim must be in formal terms: 'The ornamental design for (the article which embodies the design or to which it is applied) as shown.' If the specification properly includes a special description or modified forms, add the words 'and described' after 'shown.' The terminology in the claim's description of the article should be consistent with the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the exact formal language and ensure consistency with title and figure descriptions. Examples of claim wordings are provided in the Sample Specification and Disclosure Examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings or black & white photographs as the primary visual disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Every design patent application must include either drawings or a black and white photograph as the entire visual disclosure of the claim. The drawing or photograph must be clear and complete so nothing regarding the design is left to conjecture and must comply with 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, by including a sufficient number of views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings normally in black ink on white paper. Photographs allowed subject to 37 CFR §1.84(b)(1) and §1.152. Do not combine photographs and ink drawings in a formal submission. Photographs must not disclose environmental structure and must be limited to the claimed design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings or photographs rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Color drawings or photographs are accepted only after granting of a petition under 37 CFR §1.84(a)(2) explaining necessity, including the fee (37 CFR § 1.17(h)), three sets of color drawings/photographs, a black & white photocopy that accurately depicts the subject matter, and a required statement in the specification indicating the file contains color drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If color photographs are submitted informally and color is not part of the claimed design, add the disclaimer: 'The color shown on the claimed design forms no part thereof.' Absent such disclaimer, color will be considered an integral part of the claimed design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views: sufficiency, perspective, and omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings/photographs must contain a sufficient number of views to completely disclose the appearance of the claimed design (front, rear, right, left, top, bottom). Perspective views are suggested to show 3D appearance. Duplicate or flat views with no ornamentality may be omitted if the specification explicitly states mirror images/identities. 'Unornamented' should not describe visible surfaces that are clearly not flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If surfaces shown in perspective are fully disclosed, those surfaces normally need not be illustrated in other views. Sectional views are permissible to bring out elements of the design but not to show functional interior structure. For surface ornamentation claims, the article must be shown in broken lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface shading requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate surface shading must be used to show the character and contour of all surfaces of three-dimensional aspects and to distinguish open vs. solid areas. Solid black surface shading is not permitted except to represent the color black or color contrast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of appropriate shading may render the shape/contour nonenabling under 35 U.S.C. 112. Adding shading after filing may be viewed as introducing new matter. Use straight-line shading and stippling appropriately and do not use both on the same surface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broken line usage and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Broken lines are understood to be illustrative only and form no part of the claimed design. When used, broken lines should not intrude upon or cross the showing of the claimed design and should not be heavier than the lines used to depict the claimed design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a broken line environmental structure necessarily intrudes on the claimed design and obscures understanding, include a separate figure that discloses the claimed design without such intrusion. For surface ornamentation, the environment/article must be in broken lines to indicate it is not claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or declaration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath or declaration required of the applicant must comply with the requirements set forth in 37 CFR §1.63.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the executed oath/declaration follows regulatory format and is included in the application package in the proper order (see §1.154).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing quality and pre-filing completeness (avoid new matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing disclosure is of primary importance; it is essential that drawings or photographs be of the highest quality and conform to rules and standards. Changes to drawings after filing may introduce new matter, which is not permitted (35 U.S.C. 132).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is in the applicant's best interest to ensure drawings are clear and complete prior to filing. The Guide recommends retaining a professional draftsperson who specializes in design patent drawings. Examples of acceptable drawings are provided in the Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing process and formality acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complete application and appropriate filing fee are received, the Office assigns an application number and filing date and sends a Filing Receipt; the application is assigned to an examiner and examined in order of filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow suggested formats to ensure completeness; missing fees or required elements can prevent the application from being placed in condition for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination standards and reasons for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination entails checking for compliance with formalities, ensuring completeness of the drawing disclosure, and comparing claimed subject matter with the prior art (issued patents and published materials). Rejection may occur if disclosure is incomplete/unclear or if prior art shows the design to be unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Office action will detail rejections and may suggest amendments. Keep all Office actions for your files; do not send them back to the Office. Address each rejection specifically in any reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to Office actions: specificity and procedural items
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies must be timely and in writing, must distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the Office action, and must address every objection/rejection. A general statement that the claim is patentable without addressing how it is patentable over prior art does not comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include identifying information in all communications: application number, group art unit number, filing date, name of examiner, title of invention. Attach a Certificate of Mailing as evidence of timely mailing. If a receipt is desired, include a stamped, self-addressed postcard listing papers submitted to be date-stamped and returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration, final rejection, appeal, and continuation options
rubrics_metrics.description: After a reply, the examiner will reconsider and either withdraw the rejection and allow the application or repeat the rejection and make it Final. Applicant may file an appeal with the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences after a final rejection or after the claim has been rejected twice. Applicant may also file a new application prior to abandonment claiming benefit of the earlier filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider filing continuation applications or appealing; track reply deadlines carefully to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing example conventions (shading types, transparency, exploded and alternate views, indeterminate length, cross-sections, multiple embodiments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two common shading types: straight-line surface shading and stippling; both may be used but not together on the same surface. Elements behind transparent surfaces should be shown in light full lines. Exploded views are supplementary and must use brackets to show association. Alternate positions must be shown in separate views. Indeterminate length may be indicated by separation and a bracket. Cross-sections may be used to clarify disclosure. Multiple embodiments of a single concept may be filed in one application if appearance and shape are similar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the examples in the Guide (wristwatch, aquarium, exploded set, alternate positions, etc.) to ensure acceptable presentation. Use brackets and separation consistently to indicate intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols for draftsmen and labeling conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical symbols for conventional elements may be used on drawings when appropriate, subject to Office approval. Symbols should be clearly understood, adequately identified in the specification, and should not create confusion with other symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general, a conventional element may be shown by a labeled rectangle, square or circle; abbreviations should not be used unless their meaning is evident. Provide identification of symbols in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 35 U.S.C. and 37 CFR provisions applicable to design applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patent applications must comply with applicable statutes and regulations including (but not limited to) 35 U.S.C. 102 (novelty), 35 U.S.C. 103 (nonobviousness), 35 U.S.C. 112 (written description/enabling/no new matter), and relevant 37 CFR sections (e.g., §§ 1.3, 1.63, 1.76, 1.84, 1.121, 1.152, 1.153, 1.154, 1.155).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the full statutory and regulatory texts included at the end of the Guide and to MPEP chapter 1500 for detailed practice and procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR §1.84 and §1.152 drawing format and technical conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Design drawings must comply with § 1.84: black ink on white paper (normally), appropriate margins and 'sight' area, no holes in sheets, sheet numbering in Arabic numerals placed in the top middle (or right if necessary), view numbering with 'FIG.' and consecutive Arabic numerals, reference characters at least .32 cm (1/8 inch) in height and not placed on hatched/shaded surfaces, same reference characters used consistently, lead lines short and not crossing, corrections durable and permanent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs must meet the photographic-paper and marking requirements in §1.84; photographs and ink drawings may not be combined as formal drawings. Follow the detailed formatting rules (line weight, margins, sheet numbering, view numbering, reference character rules) to avoid formality rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and prohibition on new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the application (specification, claims, drawings) must follow 37 CFR 1.121 and related rules. No amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure. Changes to drawings must be submitted on a separate paper showing proposed changes (in red) for examiner approval; upon approval, new compliant drawings must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to specification paragraphs or sections must include clean replacement text and, when required, a marked-up version showing changes. Reinstating deleted matter requires a subsequent amendment presenting the previously deleted matter. Claim amendments must be presented in clean form and accompanied by marked-up versions showing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of application elements and specification section headings (37 CFR §1.154)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, application elements should appear in the following order: (1) design application transmittal form; (2) fee transmittal form; (3) application data sheet; (4) specification; (5) drawings or photographs; (6) executed oath/declaration. The specification should include sections in order: preamble; cross-reference to related applications; statement regarding federally sponsored research; description of figures; feature description; a single claim. Section headings should be uppercase letters without underlining or bold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the enumerated order and heading conventions to facilitate processing and examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited examination eligibility and requirements (37 CFR §1.155)
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for expedited examination, the application must include drawings in compliance with §1.84; the applicant must have conducted a pre-examination search; and the applicant must file a request for expedited examination including the fee (37 CFR §1.17(k)) and a statement that a pre-examination search was conducted including field of search and an information disclosure statement in compliance with §1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not examine an application that is not in condition for examination even if a request for expedited examination is filed (e.g., missing basic filing fee).
